verdict.tagline: An ambitious city builder struggling under heavy technical weight.
for_you_if: you love deep city building management despite bugs
you can wait for future content and expansions
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you will not tolerate save file corruption or crashes
you expect a complete feature set at launch

claims.claim: Reviewers report severe performance issues and poor optimization, citing low frame rates even on empty maps and heavy stuttering.

citations.review_text: Performance is actually worse than it was 3 years ago when it launched

Unfortunately not a good experience, Absolutely terrible optimization, and very laggy despite high efforts to try and optimise it with settings... DLC's are expensive, without DLC's there is very little to play with, traffic is an issue, simulation wasnt what I expected, and the price of this game is absurd, high, and regret immediately buying this game.

As a former Cities Skylines 1 enjoyer I unfortunately won't recommend this game. It's still a buggy mess, graphics look bad, framerate is really poor,  and LOD sucks (it's sometimes there and sometimes not). I get maximum 30 fps on a small city on my PC which is really weird. I wish this game would perform as good as first Cities game as it offers so many great additions that were just necessary. I really hope they will fix this game and make it playable. For now it's not worth 35 bucks.

I have waited 2.5 yeras to give it a try, unfortunately, the performance is horrendous, I have 30fps just in an empty map, and I needed to change resolution to FHD from my QHD diplay to make it even playable. 
And yet, the game still looks bad, the tree LODs appear if you arent zoomed in directly on them, all the roads and building look very plastic and plain.
The game looks nice if you are totally zoomed in tho, too bad thats not have you play a city builder..

Yeah you are gonna need that top tier pc lol. Didn't hit 60 fps on an empty map, bench mark like 30 fps, medium settings w/ quality dlss (Also looked like total ♥♥♥♥ with these settings ofc, probably worse than the first game lol). Also one of those games that seems to rely on dlss for anti-aliasing which would piss me off regardless of if its a game my pc can run or not, horrendous grain/visual noise if dlss is off.

Obviously didn't actually play it so negative rating isn't indicative of game quality, more of just a '♥♥♥♥ you, I'm too poor to drop 2 bands on a new gpu >:(' lol

claims.claim: Reviewers describe difficult mechanics regarding road connections, water and electricity systems, and building placement.

citations.review_text:
1.2h → 1.7h  
35 EUR -> Not so bad for this game. yeah.. buy it. It's a total new feeling from Cities Skylines 1.
This game is actually not that bad.
But the early game is extremely confusing, and it’s very easy to get stuck if you don’t understand how the new systems work.

I restarted from scratch and in 30 minutes I reached 1000 population, and the city looks genuinely amazing.
The gap between my first 1.2 hours and the next 30 minutes is huge.

---------------------------------
0h → 1.2h
Don’t buy at 50 EUR. Don’t buy at 35 EUR. Don’t buy at 10 EUR.  
This game should be free-to-play until they fix the bugs — and only then ask money for it.

I played for 1.2 hours and the experience is horrible.
Population: 85 people.
Water system: 4 water pumps.
Result: the game still cries that the water is “infected”.

The new system with water and electricity under the road is a mess. Every building complains it’s not connected to a road, and if the slope is slightly too high, the building simply refuses to connect.

And here’s the best part:
If a building can’t connect to a road, you can’t relocate it. You must delete it.

At this point I’d rather delete the game and go back to Cities Skylines 1.

Horrible, horrible experience.

I honestly didn't give this game a full chance. I refunded it based on my initial feelings of the game. It seems very developer build testing. Not a actual finished or play ready game. From difficult to place roads constant alarms on not connected wires or pipes. Or ugly building add-ons. The game felt significantly more and unneeded complication to simple build and play mechanics

claims.claim: Performance is poor and requires a powerful PC or high-end graphics card to run smoothly.

citations.review_text:
Honestly, for the terrible reputation this game has, it is pretty fun. I havent had any crazy issues with fake traffic or economy. Parking is suddenly very very important and cars will circle the city all day if they cant find a place to park. Thats a surprisingly interesting issue to fix, since parking lots and garages become a huge traffic congestion point, not just from the vehicles, but from pedestrians which block roads when they cross streets in big groups.

Anyways, if you boot it up and notice things leaving horrible ugly ghost trails as they move, turn off Nvidia DLSS completely. The game looks better without it anyways. The game is surprisingly performance heavy compared to CS1, so if you have a mid or low-end PC, it is not going to be very fun. My specs are giving me about ~50fps on medium settings with weather turned off at "big city" status. 

All in all, i like this one a lot so far. the more realistic scale makes things work a lot better, and the new road lane merging is awesome.

I have played the game more than the allotted 2 hours that Steam allows you to get your money back. They refused to help me in any way. Disappointed. The game will not run properly on my 6 month old laptop. I have played countless hours on Transport Fever 2 with no problems. The most recent problem I have had with this game (in addition to the impossible to see road building screen is that the game now crashes whenever I try to build a school or hospital. This game needs to include a message to older folks like me (80 years) that it will not work properly unless you have the correct graphics card ($300+ on Amazon). Until this mess, I was so looking forward to release of Transport Fever 3. I certainly may reconsider my purchase of that game (if it is ever released). Very disappointed in Steam.
It is very good game but it I am only recommend this game to people with high performance level devices.

Good game, but fix the laggs!! The performance of this game is trash as long as you dont have a 5,000$ PC

But IF, then its okay

I finally decided to give this game a go after hearing a lot of its launch issues had been fixed. The game is still poorly optimised and was unplayable a few hours into building a city. Unfortunately this was after the 2 hour mark, so I couldn't even get a refund. 

The gameplay itself isn't much better than CS1 and lacks a lot of the content the previous game had. While this will improve with the release of future DLC, it's going to be more expensive than CS1. The road building tool are defiantly an improvement over CS1 allowing you to do a lot more complicated things, they are nowhere near as intuitive as they were in CS1 and left me feeling frustrated at not being able to do simple things like creating circles.

Overall I wouldn't recommend CS2, unless you have access to a NASA supercomputer. I would suggest you pick up CS1 on sale and mod it for a better experience.

Good game with plenty of amazing mods that are super easy to install. The biggest downside is having to buy the add-ons all over again to get the same level of content as Cities: Skylines 1, which can be really frustrating, especially if you already owned the original game's DLC. Another thing I don't like is that neither the base game nor the new add-ons include the specialized industries or airport DLC from the previous game. The performance is also pretty poor, so you'll need a powerful PC to run the game smoothly on high settings.
good game but needs good pc

The tools for placing roads and other networks are really, really bad compared to the first game (which also had a lot of issues in this regard). Proper snapping no longer exists, especially when you want to continue an existing road/train line/bridge, instead the game makes a guess about how these networks should be connected. claims.claim: The game lacks content and building variety compared to the previous title, with repetitive structures and missing features.

citations.review_text:
I'll finally review this garbage of a game that I regrettably pre ordered years ago before it released.

Let's be completely honest what this game is, it's in the same vein of something like planet coaster, which is a sandbox painting game. In this case, cities skylines 2 is quite literally a game you play paused and that's it. 

What do I mean by that? It's the fact that compared to something like older sim cities, the city is never truly alive. It's a pseudo low effort illusion of an active city and nothing more. One thing for instance, when you build houses, they all get the same ugly rectangle high crane png, yeah I say PNG because that's what it might as well be. When you zone areas, all of them get the same exact building png where it shows a crane, and then once some time goes by, then the building automatically appears. Like, where's the life, where's the buildings being built, ANYTHING. 

You could say who cares? And I would say I do. How can this be a city builder and as per the own description of the game " With deep simulation and a living economy" when you can't get the core foundation of just building animations done, it completely takes the immersion element out of the game, not even including the fact THAT THEIR FIRST GAME HAD PROPER BUIILDING ANIMATIONS. Also to add on top of that, the building variety is terrible. Build one residential zone, and all the houses for the most part look the exact same. I'm not asking for them to make 100+ different house varieties, but for a game that's quite literally a city builder, and one of the main foundational core component of your city is PEOPLE and having HOUSES, there should be a significantly larger amount of building variety which is just not present at all.

Also they once again to try and include chirper to give "life" to your city but it's just the same rehashed garbage 3-4 tweets that just say the same thing over and over, there's a reason why people always turn that garbage off. If you've ever played …

Glowing façade, just kinda disappointing. A lot of needed improvements, QoL fixes and the inclusion of some of the first games DLC content into the base game. My biggest gripe is that the game feels so much less personal than the first one. Citizens fade in and out of existence, services like firefighters have no animations and the game lacks the different policies from the first game. It makes the game feel kinda shallow and boring to look at despite all the fancy pansy graphics. Not only that but they're STILL trying to milk you dryer than an AI data-center for their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ asset-packs and bum ass radio-stations. 

I could've said more about the things I actually liked but after 3 years they just don't deserve it. I'm HOPING that the new dev team can hold the game together. But for now you're better off pirating this or the first game with all it's 6 gazillion dlcs or just playing Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic. I'm so disillusioned with Paradox.

The gameplay itself isn't much better than CS1 and lacks a lot of the content the previous game had. While this will improve with the release of future DLC, it's going to be more expensive than CS1. The road building tool are defiantly an improvement over CS1 allowing you to do a lot more complicated things, they are nowhere near as intuitive as they were in CS1 and left me feeling frustrated at not being able to do simple things like creating circles.

Overall I wouldn't recommend CS2, unless you have access to a NASA supercomputer. I would suggest you pick up CS1 on sale and mod it for a better experience.

Underwhelming, kinda just feels like the first one made with better graphics. But just as the first game, it is very basic unless you pay for the DLC's that have all the actually enjoyable content. I don't know, just feels like another game where the developers want you to pay for the updates, just like the first game, The Sims, ATS, and any other game you can think of that just has an unnecessary amount of DLCs and Addons.

Do yourself a favor, the first game costs $20 less, just buy that one. It is just as good as this one, the graphics are just a little worse.

Been delaying purchasing this game and thought it might work well now a few years after release. Regrettable I have to say that the game is still not very stable many features I expected to be in the game was still missing. Finally, it was a poor decision to not use steam workshop mod support for this game. Better to play CS1 and save your money.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from poor optimization, frame rate drops, and lagging performance as cities grow larger.

citations.review_text: 25fps gameplay jos et omista rtx 5090 mut muuten ihan hyvä

Being a rabid fan of city simulation games, all the way back to the original SimCity that I got for the SNES, I was more than excited about CS2 after devoting hundreds of hours to CS1, even getting a new laptop before it launched. Cut to launch day and ALL the problems it had that it really put me off and was just waiting and waiting and then, finally, decided to buy it in Dec 2025. Launched it and it was OK, had a couple of crashes but i felt my Alienware m17 R5 AMD was not up to the task with around 15ish FPS.
By luck, i got my new MSI (see specs below) on July 2026 and that is when i started investing time on this game and I must say that I've had NO ISSUES AT ALL with around 110 mods installed. It launches, takes some seconds and once i am in a city, it runs with around 40 to 50 fps with a city of 85k (biggest at the moment).

Coming from CS1, you may find the games mechanics off putting but if you just take some time and patience and actually pay attention to the tutorials, you will get a hang of it. Just do not expect to come in full CS1 mode because it will just not work. There will be a learning curve but it is not insanely steep.
I believe that with all the mods I have gotten, it has made it a very different game from the vanilla but who doesn't play these games modded.
There are a lot of pros and cons but the one that i believe is the biggest PRO is the way to layout roads, it is just SO good and what I have been wanting to have forever. It is really a big game changer.
Another huge pro is the amount of detailing you can do. Just get some mods, look at some of the youtube videos and you can go crazy with as much or as little you can create. This is a really amazing part that will make you waste HOURS detailing just one block lol.
Con part, i guess it is annoying that you add bus stops and then you have to add a route, like just make it automatically. The same goes for bicycles, that you need to add bicycles stops for the cims to use the bike lanes, would b…

Need to improve the performance. GTX 3060 12GB, 64GB, AMD 5600x is freezing for some seconds , I think because the autosave, but I can see the city freezing with the zoom ,  I need to zoom out and in the see working again

im addicted to this game. also i can't run full graphics gotta upgrade my pc but it still looks good at lower graphics, sometimes its a little laggy especially with mods but it's okay, i've figured it out good game though would totally recommend if you are a cozy gamer
I'm playing on medium settings and getting 5 fps because I have a large city... the game isn't updated at all, and it was already lagging terribly even when I had a small city.
it's more fun now. wish there was more customization on the industries though
Still runs poorly after all this time.

Cities: Skylines II is a really fun game to play in your spare time. Building your city is really fun and the number of mods makes the game even better.

However, I find it annoying that save files don't save in the cloud. I play on multiple PCs/laptops, and it is always a hassle to transfer my saves. Sometimes the game glitches afterward as well. And only 40 fps is a crime, with my specs.

Otherwise, I think it is a very fun game, but cloud saves would make the experience much better.

claims.claim: Reviewers report a noticeable lack of content, features, and variety compared to the original game.

citations.review_text: The new dev team is working hard to fix architectural issues with the game, issues that should have never existed, but they have made very real progress. The issue is that the game still isn't a sequel to 1, for instance, it lacks basic traffic tweaks like the ability to make a 1-3 way stop with through traffic. How can Paradox say that this is a sequel, and a "realistic city simulator" when I don't even have the ability to make a 2-way stop sign intersection??? The traffic pathing is also completely broken, this game requires a mod called "Traffic" to fix this, but even then you have to set the pathing per intersection. You can't do zoning/districting, like at all really, so if you liked part of 1 just know that the feature isn't even in this game. You also can't create custom park districts because of this, which makes cities uglier, and less fun to build. Are any of these things going to be added in the future? Most likely, but they will probably be DLC, which is really scummy. This game will require a monumental effort to reach parity with BASE version of the first game. It's been a few years and it's still not even in a playable state. I wanna have faith in the new dev team because they've done great work so far, but the game is legit so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad that I don't really think it will ever be worth any amount of money or time.

The game is honestly great in many ways. I cant say it's torturous by any means considering I have 80 hours on it lol. Great simulation and the road building is much better than CS1 once you get the hang of it. The sims also seem to be more intelligent compared to the first. I didn't buy it at launch, but from what I see it has massively improved. HOWEVER, very disappointed in the lack of content and variety though compared to the first... This game has been in development/out for wayyyy too long for there to be such a noticeable lack of added content. Almost 3 full years in and one DLC pack :(. I keep finding myself wanting to just go back to my CS1 city. Unfortunately I can't rate it as a meh on steam, so I will *tentatively recommend the game if its on sale.* Just such a lack of content and possibilities for full price quite frankly.

the game's alright but the one thing that really bothers me is zoning and the amount of things that you can do with a district zone is way less than cs1. The selectable maps are also a bit disappointing but i guess you can download one from paradox mods. although I have a lot of critique, i do have to admit that i'm enjoying the game, and it's definitely worth trying

As of right now i can't recommend this game. not worth the value or even when its on sale. City skylines 1 is going to be an overall better experience. the models of the houses look better in the first one and there is a lot more you can do in the first one than you can the second one. 

The other thing is that the game just does not run. my computer is not bad and everything just looks bad. zoom in the cars turn into mush. zoom out the cars look like mush. and eventually the game will eventually it just drops to 18FPS. Save your money until they actually decided to make the game a game.

While I do like the asset improvements from the first game. I wish this game had more things like the first one.

claims.claim: Reviewers find that the official modding platform contains outdated or incompatible items that can cause errors, crashes, and save locks.

citations.review_text:
I played the original Cities: Skylines for years and genuinely loved it, so I was extremely excited for Cities: Skylines II. I purchased the game during its first week of release, but unfortunately, I have never been able to consistently enjoy it.

At launch, the performance was so poor that my PC could barely handle the game. Some of those issues were eventually improved, but by that point I had already uninstalled it. A few months later, I decided to give it another chance, especially after the modding platform became active.

As someone who played the original game with a large collection of mods and custom assets, modding is an essential part of the Cities: Skylines experience for me. The vanilla game simply does not provide enough variety, detail, or creative freedom to build the realistic cities many players want. Unfortunately, the modding system in Cities: Skylines II has been one of my biggest frustrations.

A large percentage of the available mods and assets are outdated or incompatible. Even when one mod is updated, it may require another dependency that is no longer supported. Installing the wrong combination can cause crashes, compatibility errors, or messages appearing in the middle of gameplay. I have even encountered situations where the game would no longer allow me to save, forcing me to close it and lose my progress.

That raises a serious question: what is the purpose of having an official modding platform when so much of its content is unreliable or outdated?

The DLC strategy has also been disappointing. Many of the paid additions feel generic, poorly designed, or lacking in meaningful content. Players clearly want more buildings, assets, architectural styles, road options, realistic services, and tools that allow cities to feel unique. Instead, the game continues to receive content that often feels limited compared with what the community has been asking for.

I also purchased one of the DLCs, only to discover that it would not appear in the g…

As someone who has literally 3,900 hours in Cities 1, I cannot recommend this game. It is so buggy, takes forever to load, and often crashes. I want to be able to play this game so bad. It just isn't where it needs to be. This is the only game on my PC that struggles to load or even work at all. It's also extremely frustrating that they removed the Workshop on Steam to create their own workshop situation. Not frustrating because they made their own, but frustrating because it hardly works/loads. 

Very disappointing.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that connecting tunnels, subways, and bridges features frustrating mechanics and overlap errors that make building infrastructure difficult.

citations.review_text:
After having played and enjoyed Cities Skylines I decided to try Cities Skylines 2.  There is a lot of new content and it is improved.  But I will say I cannot recommend this game unless it costs the same as the original.  They simply did not fix enough stupid bugs.  I cannot even open the options menu in my game anymore, I have to click f5 to save and then exit through alt tab.  That and the subways and tunnels in general still suck and are a nightmare to get to connect to each other, sometimes requiring me to delete entire loops because the last section would not connect no matter what depth I put it at.  

Things seem great at first.  But the more you play the more the bugs are the same thing they were in the original.  The more you cannot accomplish because of awful tunnel mechanics and pathfinding.  I am at the point where I have not completed one city and I am struggling to want to play more because the grand building projects I envision get messed up by bad mechanics reminiscent of the original.  

I have a bit over 40 hours into the game at time of this review.  A lot of that time is just letting it run to earn money because I was tired of building roads for low density residential which is all it seems to ask for 90% of the time.  My city is ready for bigger and better things and it only wants to build small houses.

It is ok and can be fun; but at the same time it destroys satisfaction through bad mechanics and bugs.  I do not think it is worth more than $15 in the current state.

There is a game-breaking bug where there is an overlap error when you try to bulldoze a overhead bridge across an existing road. This has been present since 2023 and as of today, the issue is still there with no fix from the developer.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that save files become corrupted, fail to load properly, or stop tracking achievement progress after extended play.

citations.review_text:
Can't unlock the Last Mile Marker achievement despite having 4 cities reach level 20 now. Looking online it seems to be a very common bug that saves will eventually stop keeping count for your achievements.
I keep trying to go back to this game hoping that they'll finally fix it, only to sink another 30 hours into a save to find that the same problems persist. Wouldn't recommend this game to anyone.

When this game works, it's pretty fun. But there's some constant issues. Frequently, save files are corrupted, the menu wont load, or when I've been playing for a while the pause menu wont open, so I can't save. I figured better specs would make the game more playable, and It has, but the underlying issues still make it off-putting. I've completely lost interest in this game, I just don't want to deal with loosing another city, or trying to recover it, or troubleshooting bugs. The fixes the new studio implemented are great, but I can't see them totally fixing the game anytime soon. Save your money and just play the original. I regret not getting a refund sooner.

Nothing ever changes with this steaming pile. You give it many, many, many, many chances to come around and just when you think maybe we're on track - crash, failure to load, busted saves, crash, excessive load times, and on and on. Don't spend good money on this and more importantly, don't waste your time building and designing and detailing and giving transportation networks logical thought to watch it all go up in smoke. I've given this game more chances than it deserves. Please don't respond by saying just "play vanilla and you can avoid the majority of the problems" This game without mods and custom assets is awful. I'm finished here.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game demands powerful computer hardware and struggles with low frame rates or simulation freezes once cities reach higher populations.

citations.review_text:
Cities Skylines II is an excellent City builder, with immense potential. It is also a terrible game. It lacks content, is infuriating to build anything in because of poor snapping and bad visual aids, depends on mods to remain interesting past the early game, and whose stability is worsened by the mods and the fact that Paradox mods is a joke of a platform. If you want to make a detailed paradise whose population doesn't exceed 50thousand, Cities Skylines 1 does it better even without its DLCs, If you want to build a megalopolis of over 500thousand, you'll struggle to crack 15fps by the time you get to that size.

I hope to see the game improve under the new stewardship of Iceflake, and while certain things have improved, it's not yet enough to justify the game's high price, for now.
Great game but needs a mega PC to do a city over 120k population

Great game overall, it grow on you and you want to spend hours city building, but unfortunately once my game reaches 60k population simulation just freezes so u are unable to play properly. Paid money for a game I can't actually play :C Unless u got a NASA pc don't touch this game. I wanna go back to CS1 now but CS2 spoiled me unfortunately :C

The reasons why I like this type of game are there but the tech problems are the reasons why I could never recommend it. 
I bought it on launch ran into problems then returned it. Bought it again after giving them enough time to fix the problems, and its playable now but doesn't come near the enjoyment of the first one. Some systems just flat out don't work properly at all. My PC that runs cyberpunk at med/high just fine, starts to struggle when a city reaches 200k. It blows my mind to see how bad this has become. Speed controls just don't work properly at all, and the traffic Ai is worse then CS1. Please do better.

The game is good but it still has lots of problems like the huge performance issues(I get max 20fps while playing), traffic is always bad no matter what you do, also the paid DLCS that should be included in the price(the game is expensive 50 euro for a unity game? WTF), other than that the game is good plus the new devs are constantly updating it and im sure theyl fix it.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that updates break mods and custom assets, resulting in corrupted save files, broken textures, and missing buildings.

citations.review_text:
For the past two years, I've been really disappointed with how this game runs and performs. I do appreciate the new studio, Ice Flake, because they seem to genuinely care about the game and have continued to improve it with regular updates. Performance has definitely gotten better overall.

That said, the game still crashes, and my mods break every time there's an update. Once again, another city I've spent countless hours building is basically ruined because the textures stopped working properly, leaving me with gray grass and missing buildings. It's honestly frustrating and disappointing.

Please find a way to let players keep using mods without every update completely breaking the game. I'm taking another break from playing until this improves.

I loved the first game, and was really excited to play this game when it first came out. Pre-purchased it and was so happy to see some of my favorite youtubers play the demo. 

Unfortunately, I can't say the same now. 

The main problem I've been having is the Creator Packs from the Paradox Mods. I have been downloading modpacks for a more texturous city, however anytime I make a save, something get's corrupted and doesn't allow me to use the mods on that save anymore. I've searched everywhere for an answer, however I can't figure out if it's my pc or the game. 

As another note, I'm not happy with how they are selling DLCs as a more "give us your money" rather than "this offers a new experience." I just wish the devs would make it as part of the base game.

citations.review_text: It's mostly fine now, except one persistent problem that has been present from purchase - Traffic errors. I don't mean traffic jams or even illogical routing, but rather cars making 3 point turns on highways and making generally strange maneuvers causing traffic chaos. I know this has something to do with a known error, but it hasn't been addressed and can be game-breaking.

I really liked the original Cities Skylines so was excided to play this sequel but was unfortunately bitterly disappointed.

Apart from things like
[list]
    [*]tools not working properly, e.g. the road-placement tool that [i]should[/i] lock roads at a 90°/180° angle having the tiniest bit of slack causing the roads to be misaligned and crooked and as a result the buildable area on either side being fractured,
    [*]drivers not having the faintest clue how a roundabout works, causing massive traffic congestion for no good reason,
    [*]not being able to build tram tracks through roundabouts or on the streets making up the roundabout,
    [*]some district policies having zero impact, like normal citizens being all too happy to cause massive traffic congestion in industrial areas just to get on the highway through the one set of on-/offramps in the industrial area instead of using the two other, much closer highway access points despite the "Gated Community"-policy being activated in the entire industrial district which [i]should[/i] prohibit anyone from entering that doesn't live or work there, or like the "Heavy Traffic Ban"-policy which doesn't deter massive semitrucks from driving through to reach different areas,
    [*]the path-finding being horrendous with some entities willing to drive into a roundabout, take the first exit at ~45°, then drive up the road for over a kilometre, turn around, drive that entire distance back down that road just to take a narrow one-way street that merges with the road from the 90° exit of said roundabout at a ~200m distance from it,

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the economic simulation has fundamental flaws, such as businesses ordering goods from outside the city while ignoring local supplies and failing to generate tax revenue.

citations.review_text: It's a decent game, but I feel like it is still half baked. The act of designing and painting a city is beautiful, but, the economic simulation is not very good. Obviously this is not Factorio but specifically the distribution and chain of goods makes no sense. The economy feels like a lie. Businesses order products from outside of the city even when the products they are looking for are right across the road. Businesses will order goods, process them rapidly, then send a truck out only after they've process all of the goods, and be down 90% of the time because they are waiting on more goods, i.e. making no profit and no tax revenue. There should be simple but more control to where companies buy goods and how much they store, warehouses aren't even in the game yet. Bottom line this is a very beautiful city painter, but not a good city builder.

You will notice I have over a hundred hours on this game, yet do not recommend it. The CURRENT state of the game is not worth $50 smackaroos, but I am hopeful this will change in the future, as Iceflake (its current developer) is making real progress on issues that have plagued the game for a LONG while.

In its current state, there are a great many bugs and simulation issues that cause problems both early and late game, as well as visual glitches, however they do seem to be working on them behind the scenes, and I look forward to seeing them finally squashed for real. Many other reviews go over this in detail, and I will admit I am not a professional on the specifics.

If you want to buy this game, DO NOT buy it at full price, at least not anytime soon. Iceflake may be making progress but they still have a lot of work ahead of them.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that base game building models lack visual variety and architectural detail, resulting in repetitive gray boxes and uniformly tall skyscrapers.

citations.review_text:
There is something fundamentally unsetteling and unsatisying about this game. It's hard to describe, unless you have played it and are a fan of city building games.

I am a huge city building game fan, so I have played many hours of this game, but there is a lot wrong with it.

-The city growth effect isn't realistic.. a game "New City" had a much better growth model, and road laying model.
-Graphics are poor, and building models are VERY poor.   In the Sim City Series, the building models were pretty well done with a lot of variety.   Cities Skylines game models are very, very poor, skyscrapers tend to grow to the same height, and they all look like grey boxes kind of.. like zero interest or effort was put into the building designs.
- Nothing seems to fit will.. proportions of buildings are very strange with most parks being enormous and other things being out of scale.
-No way to just "fill in a space" for parks.. parks don't feel like they are really a thing in this game except weird squares and circles you plop.
-Dumb "Signature Buildings" that are kind of needed to be placed or your city won't grow much
- No skyscraper growth animations  Skyscrapers just "Appear" after a crane is there.. super lame.  Skyscrapers growing is maybe the most fun part of a city building game.
-Game "atomosphere" and lighting seems strange.
- Game doesn't save almost any building models locally on your computer, so every time you load it takes forever to load the same crap.
- Hardly any older looking skyscraper models in base game, or really even one good skyscraper model
-IceFlake has fixed some stuff, but this game is fundamentally flawed, and not fun.  I think the Cities Skylines series has been a bad thing for city building games in general, because they completely misunderstand what is fun about city building games.

One of the best and worst games I have ever played at the same time. 

[b] Base Game [/b] 
The base game is quite nice, especially if you're new to City Building Games, like I was when I first purchased Cities Skylines II. However, as you learn the mechanics of the game, see other player's builds and try to up your realism, you quickly realize that the base game simply isn't enough, and lacks a lot of basic tools and assets needed to create a good-looking town. You can't move roads or assets after they've been placed, can't create canals, custom markings on roads, and other things that after having played for some time - I would deem essential.

[b] Modding [/b]
That creative frustration leads you to modding. The game has built-in software that is meant to make modding easily accessible, even for those who are not well versed in the art of customizing games. You would think, that the software being officially built in would make modding relatively easy and safe, however that's not entirely true. It is all fun and games, until you install a couple new mods and go on to open your game, all excited, just to have it crash each and every time you try to reopen. The amount of times I have uninstalled and reinstalled the game, cleaned my playsets, and started new saves is beyond me. Is there a way to avoid all this? Probably yes, but as a person that is not really fluent in computers and is too lazy and too easily frustrated to watch 5 hour long tutorials for a fix just to mess up one step and have my computer explode - it becomes really upsetting and frustrating. 

[b] Would I recommend it though? [/b]
Still, I think I would. Even with all the frustration, blood, sweat and tears I've put into making this game work. Personally, I find it so fun to just sit for hours and detail my roads and add unnecessary details, that at the end of the day, nobody will see. I do however believe that there is still a lot of things that need to be fixed, added, or tweaked to the game for me…

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the base game lacks sufficient content, building variety, and tools compared to the original title, requiring DLCs or mods to remain engaging.

citations.review_text: Honestly, not a bad game. But if you have CS1 with all the packs, just stick with that. I was really looking forward to CS2 but the base game lacks the same experience as CS1, and you have to purchase a bunch of add-ons just to get to the same level of game experience as CS1, and the add-on are terrible in comparison to the previous version. Airports and industry were my favourite things to create and manage but that level of detail is missing in CS2.

As of May 2026 I'm disappointed with city's 2, for a sequel to one of the biggest city building games its bland. They made a lot of improvements but once again are heavily relying on DLC and MODs to keep things fresh. The shear lack of options for buildings, parks, monuments, props, decals and services make every city lose its identity very fast with out mods.

Thank you Modder's for once again propping this game up with options.
